name: Alanine Transaminase
overview: Alanine Transaminase is a health topic that clinicians and patients frequently discuss during care planning in India and worldwide. Key considerations include alanine aminotransferase, formerly alanine transaminase (alt), and even earlier referred to as serum glutamate-pyruvate transaminase (gpt) or serum glutamic-pyruvic transaminase (sgpt), is a transaminase enzyme that was first characterized in the mid-1950s by arthur karmen and colleagues; alt is found in plasma and in various body tissues but is most common in the liver; it catalyzes the two parts of the alanine cycle. This summary is educational and should be paired with professional medical evaluation.
